steps.text: Cook and stir ground beef, onion, and garlic in a large skillet over medium heat until meat is crumbly and browned.
Add tomato sauce, tomato paste, salt, and oregano; stir until well combined and warmed through. Remove from heat.
Stir mozzarella, cottage cheese, and Parmesan together in a large bowl until well combined. Set aside.
Spread a layer of meat sauce onto the bottom of a slow cooker.
Add a double layer of uncooked lasagna noodles, breaking noodles to fit into the cooker as needed.
Top noodles with a portion of cheese mixture.
Repeat the layering of sauce, noodles, and cheese until all of the ingredients are used.
Cover and cook on Low until noodles are tender, 4 to 6 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Lasagna
raw_recipe.description: This crockpot lasagna is simple to make by layering a hearty ground beef and tomato sauce with lasagna noodles and 3 cheeses in the slow cooker.

video.description: See how to make a meaty lasagna in the slow cooker.

review.reviewBody: We really enjoyed this!! I did some playing around with it as others have. Replaced the cottage cheese with Ricotta and I used more tomato sauce and paste to make more of the sauce as I have one of the old crockpots that's just huge. I also put in some Italian seasoning and some roasted garlic. Just make sure that all your noodles are covered with the sauce and it will come out just great. The time was a little different for me too. It only took about 4 1/2 to 5 hours in my pot, but you have to remember that all crockpots are not the same, the size and shape can change the timing a great deal. I've made this twice now and it has come out wonderful both times. I serve it with Mama D's Italian bread (from this site) and a salad and what a meal!! Thanks Kim for a great way to make homemade lasagna without all the fuss!
If all items are preassembled and put in the 'fridge the night before, it needs to only be in the slow cooker for half the recommended time.

I used my Irish-Sicilian grandmother’s recipe for the sauce and cheese mixtures but followed this process with the crockpot. It was done in 4 hours. I just tried some and it was delicious. For the sauce, one can of stewed tomatoes and a small can of tomato paste, plus a can of water, added to a mixture of a pound of hamburger and 1/2 pound of Italian sausage with some minced onion and garlic and Italian herbs. Throw in a teaspoon of sugar to kill the acidity. I simmered it for 30 minutes. The cheese mixture is half ricotta and half cottage, chopped spinach and basil, some shredded Italian cheese blend, garlic powder, and an egg. I also sprinkled shredded mozzarella on top of each layer like this recipe called for. I have a small oval crock pot, so I didn’t use the whole 16 ounce box of noodles.

Substituted Jimmy Dean Italian sausage for ground beef. Substituted whole milk ricotta mixed with beaten egg for cottage cheese (key change). Used no-bake noodles. Added Italian blend of herbs to the cheese mixture. Added 1/2 teaspoon more to the tomato sauce mixture. Add shredded mozzarella to top at last 30 minutes, and left uncovered for last 20 minutes. Total cook time 4 hours 15 minutes. Turned out perfectly. All Clad large slow cooker.

I used a lot more sauce than the recipe called for. A 44oz. jar of Prego Italian sausage & garlic flavor, plus 1 - 15 oz.. can of tomato sauce, plus one 12oz. can of tomato paste & a can of water. Mixed it all together with a pound and a half of Italian sausage & ground pork, onions, peppers, mushrooms, garlic & Italian spices...to taste...16 oz. package of lasagna noodles, the mozzarella, ricotta & parmesan cheese. Put it all together the night before, refrigerated it, then heated it on low for a good 8 hours in my old crock pot. It came out great!! Was in no way too much sauce, covered the pasta well & didnt dry out or overcook. Family loved it & I will make it again!! Also...the reviews from other people were very helpful. Without them this recipe wouldn't have been as good. Thank you all!!

Excellent recipe! I made a couple of minor adjustments. I made 1.25 batches (which gave me 9 servings), added more spices and used spaghetti sauce instead of tomato sauce. I cooked the meat and combined the spaghetti sauce the day before and refrigerated it. This made it quick to assemble in the crockpot. I had 3 layers of noodles and added a small bit of sauce on top of the last layer of noodles before topping with cheese. The only other change I will make next time is to grease the crockpot to minimize sticking. I cooked for 3 hours in high and then 3 hours on low. Noodles cooked to a perfect softness. I will be making this again!

I made this first time today and it turned out fabulous. Only 2 of us, so I did the recipe in half. I did use a full jar of Marinara sauce ( instead of tomato sauce) 1/2 can of tomato paste to thicken and I did par boil the lasagna noodles for 5 minutes before adding to the slow cooker. It was a hit!! Thanks ! P.S. Just for reference: I have a round 4 quart slow cooker, and it's 10 yearsold!

Do NOT put any noodles on top. They will end up dried out and crusty. It would also be a good idea to prep the slow cooker by spraying PAM onto a paper towel and wiping down the sides with it. This will prevent the lasgna from sticking to the sides. Also, I used ricotta instead of cottage cheese. My wife hates cottage cheese!

TOTAL hit w/my family! I did make a few tweaks based on reviews. First off, definitely need more sauce. I used prepared spaghetti sauce (AT LEAST 2, 24 oz jars) in place of tom sauce/paste, a can of diced tomatoes, replaced cottage with ricotta (which I will also increase next time), and upped the parm/mozz cheese. Cook on low approx 5 1/2 hrs.
This was so easy and good. I used one can of tomato sauce and one can of diced tomatoes. I also added a half can of black beans to it. It only took 2 hours in my crockpot and was so good!!!

I was a little skeptical at first of making lasagna in a slow cooker, but it turned out great. The only reason I didn't give this 5 stars is that it doesn't turn out as pretty as traditional lasagna. I did make a few modifications to the recipe based on how I usually make lasagna. I did not add my meat to the sauce, I kept it separate, and I only used hot Italian sausage. I also used ricotta cheese blended with a raw egg, dried parsley, a little salt, and pepper. I also add a little hard shredded parmesan cheese to the mixture. On the day I made this I had to work later that I thought and my Crock Pot kept it on warm after the timer went off, by the time I got home the top looked burnt, but it was fine. It was dark but it tasted fine, and the top wasn't hard. I will absolutely make this again.
Easy peasy! Next time I’ll use more sauce though.

I loved the convenience of using the crockpot. I modified the recipe by using ground mild Italian sausage, and ricotta cheese, not cottage cheese. So, I used the ingredients I would use in a traditional lasagna.

i used riccotta cheese instead of cottage cheese. i also use half sausage meat or ground pork and half ground beef. I find it gives it a better flavor. It isnt pretty when you serve it but it sure tastes great.

My plans of making this in the slow cooker for dinner ended up getting changed to the oven this crazy weekend. Baked very well in the oven for 45 minutes. No changes on the recipe at all! Our son and daughter in law absolutely loved it and really enjoyed taking the leftovers home. They have added this recipe to their “dinner favorites“ list, and plan to make it routinely.
I followed the recipe with the exception using ricotta instead of cottage cheese. It was easy to make, delicious and I didn’t heat up my kitchen using the oven during a heat wave!

Followed the recipe, did not double up the noodles, just a single layer, but 4 single layers total in a standard crock. Did pour 1¼c water into the crock after assembly. Did season the meat sauce to my liking. Started crock on high until I put the lid on, then switched to low, took about four hours. The ingredients list isn't very long, yet the flavor is very good. I think there's a big flavor boost from cooking the pasta with the meat sauce. Will definitely make again, it came together pretty quickly.
I cooked this for 6 hours on low. My top noodles were al dente. Overall my husband and I enjoyed this. If you have a busy day planned, this is a great solution. Will make this again.

I made this to meal prep. I used lots of mozzarella and substituted Colby cheese in place of cottage cheese. I also added fresh spinach. I used just enough spaghetti sauce to mix the meat mixture. It cooked through in 3 hours. I won’t make lasagna any other way from now on! This recipe was easy to follow and as delicious as it looks.
SUCH an easy recipe! My only advice (depending on your slow cooker) is to cook closer to 4 hours than 6. I cooked mine for 5 hours and the edges were just a little to crispy.
